title: The Covenant Names
summary: King Benjamin takes the names of those who entered a covenant with God. All except little children have entered the covenant and taken upon them the name of Christ.
characters: the people who entered the covenant

explicit_facts.text: King Benjamin considered it expedient to take the names of those who had entered a covenant with God to keep his commandments.
All except little children had entered the covenant and taken upon them the name of Christ.

reasonable_visual_inferences: A record or list could represent the names being taken.
unspecified_visual_details: The method of taking names and the appearance of any record are not stated.

narration.text: take the names of all those who had entered into a covenant with God
there was not one soul, except it were little children

prohibited_inventions: Do not depict God or Christ appearing; the verses describe a covenant and taking Christ’s name, not a visible appearance.

title: Mosiah Consecrated
summary: After finishing these things, King Benjamin consecrates his son Mosiah as ruler and king, gives him charges concerning the kingdom, and appoints priests to teach the people. He dismisses the multitude, and they return by families to their homes.

explicit_facts.text: King Benjamin consecrated his son Mosiah to be ruler and king over the people and gave him charges concerning the kingdom.
King Benjamin appointed priests to teach the people and remind them of their oath.
King Benjamin dismissed the multitude, and they returned by families to their homes.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The consecration, charges, and appointment take place before the multitude is dismissed.
unspecified_visual_details: The ceremony, the setting, and the appearance or number of the priests are not specified.

narration.text: had consecrated his son Mosiah to be a ruler and a king over his people

prohibited_inventions: Do not invent the contents of the kingdom’s charges or the priests’ teaching.

title: Mosiah Begins to Reign
summary: Mosiah begins to reign in his father’s stead at age thirty. The account places this at about 476 years after Lehi left Jerusalem.

explicit_facts.text: Mosiah began to reign in his father’s stead at age thirty.
The account gives the elapsed time since Lehi left Jerusalem as about 476 years.

unspecified_visual_details: The place and manner in which Mosiah’s reign began are not specified.

narration.text: Mosiah began to reign in his father’s stead.
in the thirtieth year of his age

prohibited_inventions: Do not depict Lehi as present; he is mentioned only as a time reference.

title: Benjamin’s Death
summary: King Benjamin lives three years and dies.

explicit_facts.text: King Benjamin lived three years and died.

unspecified_visual_details: The circumstances, place, and visual details of his death are not stated.

narration.text: king Benjamin lived three years and he died.

prohibited_inventions: Do not depict a cause or manner of death not given in the verse.

title: Mosiah’s Observance
summary: Mosiah walks in the ways of the Lord, observes the Lord’s judgments and statutes, and keeps the commandments given to him.

explicit_facts.text: Mosiah walked in the ways of the Lord, observed his judgments and statutes, and kept his commandments.

unspecified_visual_details: The verse does not specify a particular action, place, or visible divine appearance.

did keep his commandments in all things

title: The King and the Fields
summary: King Mosiah causes his people to till the earth and tills it himself so he will not burden them, following his father’s example. No contention occurs among the people for three years.

explicit_facts.text: King Mosiah caused his people to till the earth and also tilled it himself so he would not become burdensome to them.
Mosiah acted according to what his father had done.
There was no contention among the people for three years.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Tilling the earth can be shown as agricultural labor.
unspecified_visual_details: The crops, tools, landscape, and the specific people working with Mosiah are not stated.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The three-year period without contention is reported, not a separately described event.
